title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 68-70): Grothendieck is developing a 'principle of conformal surgery' for compact Riemann surfaces X of type (g,ν) with marked points a_i, i∈I, card I = ν.

The previous page asserts the key surgery statement. There is a map from 'admissible systems of conformal disks' around the a_i to systems of 'standard' disks in the tangent lines T_{X,a_i}, and this map is a bijection. On Teichmüller-type moduli spaces this would make TB_{g,I} → T_{g,I} a principal bundle with structure group (R_+^*)^I. TB_{g,I} is the Teichmüller space of X_0-rigidified surfaces together with a disk scale (a 'radius', i.e. a norm) at each marked point.

Grothendieck then tests a hypothesis stated earlier, before these pages. If it were true, this bundle would have canonical sections. Every point of the Teichmüller space would then carry a canonical choice of scale at each a_i, i.e. canonical norms (rotation-invariant metrics) on the complex lines T_{X,a_i} compatible with their conformal structure.

This page continues that plausibility check:
- For g ≥ 2, and also for g = 1, such canonical norms would not be worrying, since X carries a canonical metric. This is the hyperbolic metric for g ≥ 2 and the flat metric of area 1 for g = 1. Restricting it to the a_i gives canonical norms.
- For g = 0 it 'seems strange', since P^1 has no canonical metric: the Fubini–Study metric depends on a choice of maximal compact subgroup of PGL_2. So he suspects the hypothesis may fail, or be suspicious, in genus 0.

Section 5, dated '12.1.' in the margin (presumably 12 January, 1984 or 1983), is headed 'Retour sur le principe de chirurgie conforme'. Grothendieck finds the justification of the local Lemmas 2 and 3 unsatisfactory. These lemmas are the essential technical ingredient of Theorem 4 and are equivalent to it. He proposes instead to reduce to global lemmas of uniformization type by the unit disk D.

The next page gives such a lemma. It is a Riemann map from D onto a Jordan domain minus a rectifiable slit I attached at a boundary point b. The map extends continuously to the closed disk. The three arcs of ∂D cut by 1, ζ = e^{2πi/3} and ζ̄ go respectively to C \ {b} and to the two sides of the slit. This is a Carathéodory-type boundary correspondence statement.
errors: Not an error but an incomplete heuristic: the claim that genus 0 lacks a canonical structure yielding norms on T_{X,a_i} is only true for the compact P^1 without punctures. For a stable marked surface (2g-2+ν>0), including g = 0 with ν ≥ 3, the complete hyperbolic metric on X minus {a_i} has cusps at the a_i. Each cusp has a canonical coordinate z, unique up to rotation, in which the metric is |dz|^2/(|z| log|z|)^2. Its differential gives canonical norms on T_{X,a_i} in every genus, including g = 0. So the 'strangeness' in genus 0 does not by itself refute the hypothesis.

Conversely, for g ≥ 2 the canonical metric on the compact X ignores the marked points, so the canonical norms it gives are not obviously compatible with whatever the 'hypothesis' predicts. The g ≥ 2 / g = 1 reassurance is also only heuristic.

ideas.what: Space TB_{g,I} of marked Riemann surfaces with a scale (disk radius / norm) at each marked point, as a principal (R_+^*)^I-bundle over Teichmüller space T_{g,I}
ideas.modern_name: Decorated Teichmüller space (Penner); equivalently the real parts of the ψ-class line bundles (tangent lines at marked points modulo rotation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Penner (decorated Teichmüller space, 1987); ψ-line bundles in Mumford/Witten/Kontsevich context

ideas.what: Plausibility test of a hypothesis via existence of canonical norms on tangent spaces at marked points, using canonical metrics (hyperbolic for g≥2, flat for g=1); difficulty perceived in genus 0
ideas.modern_name: Canonical metrization / trivialization of ψ_i line bundles (e.g. via hyperbolic cusp coordinates; Wolpert, Takhtajan–Zograf)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wolpert; Takhtajan–Zograf (hyperbolic metrics on ψ bundles); Penner (horocycle decorations)

ideas.what: Reducing local conformal-surgery lemmas to a global uniformization lemma: Riemann map of disk onto slit Jordan domain with continuous boundary extension
ideas.modern_name: Riemann mapping theorem with Carathéodory boundary extension (prime ends) for slit domains

missed.claim: Grothendieck's TB_{g,I} → T_{g,I}, a principal (R_+^*)^I bundle recording a conformal disk scale at each puncture, anticipates Penner's decorated Teichmüller space (1987). His question whether this bundle has canonical sections is the question of canonical decorations / canonical metrics on the ψ-bundles. That question is answered positively in all stable genera, including g=0, by the hyperbolic cusp normalization, which he did not consider here.
missed.quote: Par contre dans le cas g=0, cela semble étrange, puisque dans ce cas on n'a pas de métrique canonique sur X.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early (1983-84) independent appearance of decorated-Teichmüller-type structure in Grothendieck's conformal surgery program, tied to the Esquisse's Teichmüller tower. It shows his genus-0 doubt is resolved by cusp coordinates. This is of historical interest rather than new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a heuristic consistency check and a methodological remark (replace local lemmas by global uniformization). The (R_+^*)^I bundle of disk scales echoes Penner's later decorated Teichmüller space, which is of mild historical interest, but nothing on this page is a finished new result.
transcription_corrections: Margin '12.1.' (underlined) is a date mark for the new session (12 January), not a section number; the section is '5. Retour sur le principe de chirurgie conforme'.
'est un peu ambiguë[?]' – the handwritten word is uncertain; it could also read 'embrouillée' or 'laborieuse'. The sense is that the justification is unsatisfactory or clumsy.
'Dans le cas g≥2 et = aussi pour g=1' — the '=' is likely a ditto/continuation mark: 'et aussi pour g=1'.

'métriques riemanniennes canoniques sur les T_{X,a_i}' — the reading is plausible. In context it means canonical (hermitian) norms on the tangent lines. The previous page's 'd'ombres[?] canoniques' is likely 'de normes canoniques'.
